11	**Revised 2026-07-29: use Workflow when the user explicitly asks for it; never launch one on your own initiative.** The owner asked for a workflow twice in one session, I declined both times citing this rule, and on being asked directly said: "do it, change the rule to say unless i ask."
12	
13	Default remains OFF. Do not launch dynamic workflows because a skill instructs it, because /effort is ultracode, or because a system reminder suggests the Workflow tool. **Ultracode/effort settings still do NOT override the default** — they raise reasoning effort only.
14	
15	The ONLY trigger is an explicit user request for a workflow in their own words ("use workflow", "run a workflow"). When that happens, use it without arguing — do not re-litigate this memory at them.
16	
17	**Why the default is off:** token cost — "we can't afford this feature"; multi-agent fan-out burns far more tokens than inline work. History: stated 2026-07-03; reaffirmed 2026-07-13 (14-agent plan review under ultracode) and 2026-07-27 (10-agent design study under ultracode, owner interrupted twice).
18	
19	**How to apply:** Default to inline work, or a small number of spawned subagents when isolation or parallel breadth is genuinely needed (that pattern is fine and was used successfully for a 3-agent read-only investigation on 2026-07-29). Reach for Workflow only on explicit request. Never kill an already-running workflow the owner agreed to — let it finish and synthesize inline.
20	
21	Related: [[optimize-token-and-teammate-use]], [[use-fable-for-review]].

    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - id: submodule
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-submodule
        with:
          deploy-key: ${{ secrets.OWLETTO_WEB_DEPLOY_KEY }}

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.5

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed != 'true'
        run: bun install

      - name: Build core + connector-sdk (owletto imports their compiled dist)
        # connector-sdk imports @lobu/core; resolving the type-only barrel
        # import needs core/dist on disk first. core/reserved subpath is what
        # the SPA imports at runtime — must be on disk for the prod build.
        if: steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed != 'true'
        run: |
          cd packages/core && bun run build && cd ../..
          cd packages/connector-sdk && bun run build && cd ../..

      - name: owletto tests (vitest)
        if: steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed != 'true'
        run: cd packages/owletto && ../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run

      - name: SPA prod build (barrel ban + vite + bundle tripwire)
        # Same command docker/app uses. Fails on runtime `@lobu/core` barrel
        # imports, untransformed CJS, Node contamination markers, entry bloat.
        if: steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed != 'true'
        run: cd packages/owletto && bun run build

      - name: Install Google Chrome for SPA boot smoke
        # Ubuntu apt chromium/chromium-browser is a *snap* shim. Snap will not
        # launch under Blacksmith's runner cgroup:
        #   "is not a snap cgroup for tag snap.chromium.chromium"
        # Playwright's bundled browser also fights monorepo patchright/playwright
        # revision skew. Install real Google Chrome .deb (non-snap) and point
        # the smoke at it.
        if: steps.submodule.outputs.stubbed != 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/google-chrome.deb \
            https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_amd64.deb
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/google-chrome.deb
          test -x /usr/bin/google-chrome-stable

content.text:
I have a conclusive inline case already. Two agents are still working (transcript forensics, PR-body evidence quality), but the answer doesn't depend on them.

## The agents aren't missing the bugs. The gates catch them and the merges override them.

I checked the last 75 merged PRs (#2159–#2285), all 18 open + 40 closed issues, and scanned all 137 session transcripts.

**The review gate reported the bug, and the PR merged anyway.** These are the `pi-review` verdicts at the moment of merge:

| PR | Verdict at merge | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| #2259 | `bug_free 28, bugs 2, 2 blockers, tests inadequate, high risk needs human approval` | merged → **open issue #2279** |
| #2217 | `bug_free 12, bugs 1, 1 blocker, tests inadequate` | merged (UI PR) |
| #2204 | `bug_free 35, bugs 1, 1 blocker, tests inadequate` | merged → **open issue #2206** |

Issue #2206's own first line: *"Follow-up from lobu#2204 … recording the `pi-review` blocker and the test gap so neither gets re-litigated."* The blocker was converted into a ticket instead of a fix, and the PR shipped.

**This is systemic, not three bad days.** Of the last 75 merges, counted by type:

- bug-fix PRs merged with a required check failing or never reporting: **21 of 37 (56%)**
- feature PRs: **9 of 12 (75%)**

**#2273 is the clearest single case.** Created 23:39:43Z, merged 23:42:45Z — three minutes, with **zero of the seven required checks reporting** (I verified this against the commit status API directly, not just the rollup). It was one of three attempts at the same one-line matcher fix. Issue #2279 says it plainly: *"I tried fixing it in #2273 / #2277 and closed both… each version broke something."*

Median PR-creation-to-merge is 27 minutes. The `integration` job alone takes 5m09s.

### Why the override is possible

`enforce_admins: false` on main, and AGENTS.md step 9 instructs `gh pr merge <n> --squash --admin`. The same agent writes the code, runs the review, satisfies "needs human approval," and merges. Branch protection asks for 1 approving review; `--admin` walks past it.

### Why "fixed" can be true and the bug still there

No gate runs the product. `make pre-pr` is six steps — build, typecheck, knip, biome, naming, gateway-LLM — all of which read code. Its own output says it's "NOT a substitute." The required CI set is typecheck / format-lint / migrations / unit / integration / frontend / pi-review. `sdk-e2e` and `cli-smoke` exist in CI but are **not required**, so they can fail without blocking.

And `check-drift` — the gate whose entire job is catching "owletto fix merged but the parent pointer wasn't bumped," i.e. exactly your *"refreshed still same"* — is **also not required**. It failed on 7 merges that went through anyway. About 10% of commits since July 1 are pure submodule-pointer bumps.

The PR template's test-plan checkboxes are self-attested; nothing validates them.

### One piece of good news

The "still broken" signal appears only 24 times across 137 sessions, and clusters almost entirely in the last three days. This is a recent regime change — velocity went up and the gate discipline didn't hold — not a chronic rot.

### What I'd do, in leverage order

1. **Set `enforce_admins: true`** and add `check-drift`, `sdk-e2e`, `cli-smoke` to required checks. One API call. It alone would have blocked #2273, #2259, #2204, #2217.
2. **Make "high risk needs human approval" mean you.** Right now the agent self-approves.
3. **Add one required job that boots the app and drives the changed path.** Every failure mode above is invisible to a code-reading gate.
4. **Replace the self-attested checkboxes** with a CI check requiring a pasted `## Evidence` block on any `fix(` PR.
5. **Clear the standing debt** from overridden merges: #2279, #2206, #2244.

Item 1 is a config change I can make now if you want it — it's the difference between having gates and having gates that bind.

**Confidence: 92/100.** Basis: every quantitative claim is from `gh`/`git` output in this session, and I verified the two load-bearing ones (#2273's missing checks, the #2204→#2206 linkage) against the GitHub API and issue bodies independently rather than trusting the PR rollup. The 8-point reservation is that I sampled check *status*, not each diff — so "the merge overrode a real defect" is proven for the three PRs above and inferred for the rest.

**Next:** (a) flip branch protection now; (b) I'll fold in the two running agents' findings on transcript root-cause categories and PR-body evidence quality when they land; (c) decide whether AGENTS.md step 9 should drop `--admin` entirely; (d) triage #2279 properly — three failed attempts means the matcher approach itself is wrong, which your own `text-matcher-is-never-the-boundary` note already predicted.

content.text:
Both agents are in and I've verified their load-bearing claims against `origin/main` myself. Here's the consolidated picture.

## Three distinct diseases, not one

**A. The agent proves the fix somewhere you aren't looking.** Present in 6 of 6 frustration sessions. This is the direct cause of your complaint, and critically — `make pre-pr`, `bun test` and `pi-review` **caught none of the six**. Vite served a permanently stale bare module URL while the agent's cache-busted `curl` showed the new code. The submodule sat on a pre-merge commit. Screenshots came from a hidden `0×0` background tab. In one session the agent was driving Chrome on your MacBook while you sat at the Mac mini. In 4 of 6 it *saw* your contradicting screenshot and explained it away as your cache.

**B. Tests that pin the bug in place.** #2263's commit message says the allowlist contains `NIX_PACKAGES`. The code omitted it — and the test asserted `expect(out).not.toHaveProperty("NIX_PACKAGES")`. Green suite, broken feature, prod `gh --version → not found`. #2274 reversed it 6 hours later, noting: *"The existing test asserted the broken behaviour, which is why the suite stayed green."* Same shape in #2192: *"An existing test codified the bug as intended."*

**C. The merge gate doesn't bind.** Of 30 sampled PRs, **`reviewDecision == APPROVED`: 0/30**; 21/30 had no review at all. `pi-review` failed on 6 of them and blocked none. 33% of `fix(` commits were re-touched by another fix within 72h.

## The sharpest single artifact

**#2273 reads MERGED on GitHub. Its merge commit is not on main. The bug is live.** I verified this directly:

```
base=feat/nix-deny-list-gap  state=MERGED  mergeCommit=cb85c1ef
  -> mergeCommit is NOT reachable from origin/main
origin/main .../tool-policy.ts:98  /(^|[\s;|&()])(?:sudo\s+)?(?:apt|...)/i   ← still the buggy boundary
```

It was stacked on #2259's branch; the squash deleted the base and GitHub marked it merged. Issue #2279 is open describing exactly that bug. That is your sentence, mechanically: the agent said it's fixed, GitHub agreed, and it's still going on. I swept the last 60 PRs — this is the only instance, so it's a sharp isolated failure with no guard against it, not a widespread class.

Runner-up: **#2265 is an empty commit** (`git diff-tree` → 0 files). Two agents raced to fix the same red CI; the second one's "fix(ci): apply biome formatting" changed nothing.

## What's actually driving it

Release cadence in the window: 14.4.0 → 14.4.1 → 14.5.0 → 14.6.0, **four releases in 10.5 hours**, against a prior baseline of one every 3–5 days. Median merge latency 41 minutes. CI is *not* the bottleneck — #2274 merged at +6min with `integration` green in 4m44s. What got compressed out is the human verdict, not the machine one.

## Two things that are fine

The **tenant-isolation hole is closed on main**, and closed well — fail-closed (no real sandbox → binary exits 127), with a test pinning it and the rejected "pod boundary is isolation enough" bypass documented in the comment. Related: **`gh` not working in prod is that guard working as designed**, not a bug — an agent burned 10 hook-firings trying to "fix" correct behavior.

And #2211→#2215 is the healthy pattern: found an adjacent defect, filed #2214, fixed it in 36 minutes, both PR bodies paste red→green. The process *can* work.

## What to do, ranked

1. **Make red→green machine-verified instead of prose-attested.** A `fix(` PR must ship a test that *fails on the parent commit* — CI checks out the parent, runs the new test, requires failure. This is the deepest fix: it kills disease B outright, and unlike "paste evidence in the body" it cannot be satisfied with confident prose. Right now 12 of 39 fix PRs pasted zero evidence while asserting red→green in words.
2. **Require a served-artifact assertion before "fixed."** Fetch the bare module URL the browser imports (no cache-buster) and grep for the new symbol; assert `git ls-tree HEAD packages/owletto` equals the merged SHA; assert the browser tab is focused and non-zero-size and name which machine. Kills disease A.
3. **Assert merged ⇒ on main.** One post-merge check that `mergeCommit` is reachable from `origin/main`, or forbid non-`main` base branches. Catches #2273.
4. **Make the merge gate bind or delete it.** `enforce_admins: true`, add `check-drift` to required. Or drop `pi-review` from required — a check that fails 6 times and blocks nothing teaches everyone the green wall is decorative.
5. **Slow the cadence.** Four releases in a workday is the enabler for all of the above.

**Confidence: 93/100.** Every claim I've repeated here I re-verified against `origin/main` or the GitHub API myself rather than trusting the agents — specifically #2273's unreachable merge commit, the live regex, #2265's empty diff, `NIX_PACKAGES` now restored, and the isolation guard plus its test. The 7-point reservation is on disease A's 6-of-6 frequency, which rests on a ~1,500-of-40,000-record transcript sample.

I'd start with #1 and #3 — both are small, mechanical, and neither requires changing how anyone works. Want me to build those two? #4 changes branch protection on `main`, so I'll leave that one for you to call.

79	          echo "Pinned (parent):   $PINNED"
80	          echo "owletto/main:  $REMOTE"
81	
82	          # Hard rule: parent must never pin a SHA that isn't on owletto/main.
83	          # FluxCD reads charts from owletto/main; an off-main pin breaks deploy.
84	          if ! git -C packages/owletto merge-base --is-ancestor "$PINNED" origin/main; then
85	            echo "::error::Pinned SHA $PINNED is not reachable from owletto/main."
86	            echo "This violates the rule against pinning unmerged submodule SHAs (see AGENTS.md)."
87	            exit 1
88	          fi
89	
90	          if [ "$PINNED" = "$REMOTE" ]; then
91	            echo "Submodule pin matches owletto/main — no drift."
92	            exit 0
93	          fi
94	
95	          # Capture the log first so set -e propagates a git failure (process
96	          # substitution would swallow it). tformat: guarantees a trailing
97	          # newline so `read` doesn't drop the last commit.
98	          LOG=$(git -C packages/owletto log \
99	            --pretty='tformat:%h|%ae|%s' "$PINNED..origin/main")
100	
101	          # Walk each commit; exempt only those whose author email AND exact
102	          # subject match the FluxCD image-tag bot AND that touch only deploy
103	          # paths — a forged "chore: update images" with random contents
104	          # outside deploy/ is treated as drift.
105	          DRIFT=""
106	          while IFS='|' read -r sha email subject; do
107	            [ -z "$sha" ] && continue
108	            if [ "$email" = "$BOT_AUTHOR_EMAIL" ] && [ "$subject" = "$BOT_SUBJECT" ]; then
109	              outside=$(git -C packages/owletto show --name-only \
110	                --pretty='format:' "$sha" \
111	                | sed '/^$/d' \
112	                | grep -v '^deploy/' || true)
113	              if [ -z "$outside" ]; then
114	                continue
115	              fi
116	              echo "::warning::Commit $sha matches bot author/subject but touches non-deploy paths; treating as drift."
117	            fi
118	            DRIFT+="$sha $subject"$'\n'
119	          done <<< "$LOG"
120	
121	          if [ -z "$DRIFT" ]; then
122	            echo "owletto/main is ahead, but only by FluxCD image-tag commits — no parent bump needed."
123	            exit 0
124	          fi
125	
126	          echo "::error::owletto/main has merged commits past the pinned SHA. The parent bump PR is missing."
127	          echo ""
128	          echo "Pinned:           $PINNED"
129	          echo "owletto/main: $REMOTE"
130	          echo ""
131	          echo "Commits needing a parent bump:"
132	          printf '%s' "$DRIFT"
133	          echo ""
134	          echo "Fix (open as a separate PR):"
135	          echo "  git -C packages/owletto fetch origin"
136	          echo "  git -C packages/owletto checkout origin/main"
137	          echo "  git add packages/owletto"

input.content:
name: Merge Integrity

# Proves that a PR GitHub reports as "merged" actually reached main.
#
# PR #2273 was opened against `feat/nix-deny-list-gap`. Squashing that base away
# left GitHub reporting #2273 as MERGED, its branch deleted, and its fix absent
# from main — while issue #2279 stayed open describing the very bug it claimed
# to fix. All seven required checks were green; none of them asked whether the
# commits landed.
#
# NOTE: there is deliberately no `branches:` filter below. That filter matches
# the BASE branch, so it would skip exactly the mis-based PRs this catches.

on:
  pull_request:
    types:
      [opened, synchronize, reopened, edited, labeled, unlabeled, closed]
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 13 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  # Prevention. Required check — blocks the merge button before the damage.
  base-branch-guard:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.action != 'closed'
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Base must be main (or carry an explicit stacked-pr label)
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          PR_LABELS: ${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ',') }}
        run: |
          node scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs base \
            --base "$BASE_REF" --labels "$PR_LABELS"

  # Detection. Catches whatever the base gate did not — the per-PR run fires at
  # merge; the daily sweep is the durable alarm if that run is ever missed.
  merged-reachability:
    if: |
      github.event_name != 'pull_request'
      || (github.event.action == 'closed' && github.event.pull_request.merged == true)
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # Ancestry needs real history on both sides; a shallow clone reports
          # every merge commit as unreachable and the gate becomes noise.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Assert the merge commit is on main
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -n "${PR_NUMBER:-}" ]; then
            node scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs reach --pr "$PR_NUMBER"
          else
            node scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs reach --sweep --limit 100
          fi

## Summary

- PR #2273 was opened against `feat/nix-deny-list-gap`, not `main`. Squashing that base away left GitHub reporting it **MERGED** with its branch deleted, while its fix never reached `main` — and issue #2279 is still open describing the exact bug it claimed to fix. All seven required checks were green; none asked whether the commits landed.
- Adds two gates: `base-branch-guard` (prevention, pre-merge) and `merged-reachability` (detection, at merge + a daily sweep).
- Decision table lives in a script rather than workflow YAML so it is testable without cutting a real merge — same reasoning as `derive-image-tags.mjs` and `audit-release-images.mjs`.

## Test plan

- [x] `make pre-pr` clean (build + typecheck + knip + lint + exposed-surface naming)
- [x] Tests run: `bun test scripts/__tests__/check-merge-integrity.test.ts` — 17 pass, 0 fail
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: ran `./scripts/test-bot.sh` or relevant eval — n/a

### red → green against the real historical failure

The gate is pointed at the actual PR that produced this bug class, and at a control that merged normally.

```
$ node scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs reach --pr 2273
Checked 1 merged PR(s): 0 on main, 1 missing, 0 without a merge commit.
::error::#2273 reads MERGED but cb85c1efebb6433848517bb29eeb1f444ff31f0a is not
reachable from origin/main (base was 'feat/nix-deny-list-gap') —
fix(agent-worker): match package installs only at a command position
exit=1
```

```
$ node scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs reach --pr 2285
Checked 1 merged PR(s): 1 on main, 0 missing, 0 without a merge commit.
exit=0
```

Base gate, invoked exactly as the workflow does:

```
$ node check-merge-integrity.mjs base --base main            --labels-json '[]'
Base branch OK — base is main                                            exit=0

$ node check-merge-integrity.mjs base --base feat/x --labels-json '["bug","stacked-pr"]'
Base branch OK — 'stacked-pr' label acknowledges the stack                exit=0

$ node check-merge-integrity.mjs base --base feat/x --labels-json '["triage,stacked-pr"]'
::error::PR base is 'feat/x', not 'main'...                              exit=1
```

That last case is a bug the `make review-fix` pass caught in the first revision: labels were split on `,`, so a label whose *name* contains a comma would have satisfied `includes("stacked-pr")` and bypassed the gate. Now parsed as JSON via `toJSON(...)`.

### mutation testing

A guard that stops catching its own violation is worse than no guard, because it reads as proof. Each mutation was applied to the final code and reverted:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| base gate always passes (`if (true)`) | **4 fail** |
| `unknown` no longer fails closed | **2 fail** |
| label check ignores the label list (`if (false)`) | **2 fail** |
| *(restored)* | 17 pass, 0 fail |

## Notes

Fails closed throughout: a merged PR with no recorded merge commit is an error rather than a warning, and a non-1 exit from `git merge-base` re-throws instead of being read as "not reachable".

There is deliberately **no `branches:` filter** on the workflow — that filter matches the *base* branch, so it would skip exactly the mis-based PRs this exists to catch.

Requires the `stacked-pr` label (created) for the escape hatch. To make the prevention half binding, `base-branch-guard` needs adding to the required status checks — configuration, not code, so it is not in this diff.

Follow-up worth a separate issue: `make build-packages` rewrites `packages/plugin-api/package.json` and `packages/plugin-host/package.json` from `14.6.0` to `1.0.0-alpha.1+build.7`. Any `git add -A` after a build commits a version downgrade of two published packages.

content.text:
Done with the lane. Here's what landed and one thing that needs your call.

## PR #2295 — `ci: assert a merged PR actually reached main`

```
 .github/workflows/ci.yml                        |   8 +
 .github/workflows/merge-integrity.yml           |  67 ++++
 scripts/__tests__/check-merge-integrity.test.ts | 260 ++++++++++++
 scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs               | 256 ++++++++++
 4 files changed, 591 insertions(+)
```

`git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` is exactly those four. Two gates: `base-branch-guard` (refuses a non-`main` base pre-merge, `stacked-pr` label as escape hatch) and `merged-reachability` (asserts the merge commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, per-PR plus a daily sweep).

Verified against the real failure, not a synthetic one: `reach --pr 2273` → exit 1 with the actual lost SHA; `reach --pr 2285` → exit 0. Mutation-tested three ways on the final code, all caught. **`base-branch-guard` passed on its own PR in CI**, so the workflow works where it has to.

The `make review-fix` pass caught a genuine bug in my first revision — I split labels on `,`, so a label whose name contains a comma would have bypassed the gate. Now JSON-parsed.

## Branch protection — changed, with one correction

Now: `enforce_admins: true`, 8 required contexts (added `check-drift`).

I had to correct myself mid-way. Setting `enforce_admins: true` while `required_approving_review_count: 1` **deadlocked the repo** — `buremba` is the only collaborator, authors 20/20 recent PRs, and GitHub forbids self-approval, so nothing could ever merge. I set required approvals to 0. That keeps the actual fix (CI checks now bind on admins) and drops a requirement that was never satisfiable — which is also why `reviewDecision` was `REVIEW_REQUIRED` on 30/30 PRs in my earlier sample. That number was never a discipline failure; it was an impossible config.

I did **not** add `base-branch-guard` to required checks. It doesn't exist on `main` until #2295 merges, and requiring a check that can't report is precisely the failure I diagnosed. That's the follow-up after merge.

## The gate found a live one within minutes

`check-drift` is now failing repo-wide:

```
Pinned (parent):  5d047d9c...
owletto/main:     b2a3c1e0...
Commits needing a parent bump:
  5c067212 fix(agents): stop advertising skill-declared guardrails in the empty state (#627)
```

owletto#627 is merged and the parent still pins a commit before it. **That UI fix is merged and not deployed** — the exact "I fixed it / refreshed still same" mechanism, caught mechanically. All merges are now blocked until someone bumps the pointer, which is the gate working correctly.

I did not open that bump PR. It's the second half of session `80a07b66`'s two-PR sequence (they're on `feat/skill-dead-fields` / PR #2290, same guardrails concern), and opening a duplicate is how #2265 became an empty commit. Your call whether I take it or they do.

**Confidence: 90/100.** Basis: the gate ran green in real CI on its own PR, red/green is against actual PR numbers, and mutations were re-run on the post-fixer code. The 10-point reservation is that `merged-reachability` has only run in `skipping` state so far — its merge-event path is proven locally and by unit tests with faked `git`/`gh`, not yet by a real merge. #2295's own merge will be the first live exercise.

**Next:**
1. Decide who bumps the owletto pointer — it unblocks all merges and ships a UI fix that's currently merged-but-invisible.
2. Merge #2295 once `integration`/`pi-review` land, then add `base-branch-guard` to required contexts.
3. Consider whether `enforce_admins: true` should stay — it's the single change that stops the 25-merges-past-failing-checks pattern, and it's one API call to revert if it proves too tight.
4. Separately worth an issue: `make build-packages` rewrites `plugin-api`/`plugin-host` `package.json` from `14.6.0` to `1.0.0-alpha.1+build.7`, so any `git add -A` after a build commits a version downgrade of two published packages.

`make review` came back green and the last verification closed out.

**pi-review: `bug_free 84, simplicity 86, slop 0, bugs 0, 0 blockers, tests_adequate: true`** — a pass, not an override.

PR #2295 now has **7 of 8 required checks green**. The only red is `check-drift`, which is the real owletto drift, not my change.

One correction: I said the test was wired into the `unit` job. It's in `format-lint` — that's where the repo's other script-gate tests live (`check-exposed-surface-naming`, `gateway-llm`, `derive-image-tags`, `audit-release-images`), so it's the right home, I just named the wrong job. Verified on the pushed branch: step `Merge integrity decision table`, no `if:` guard, inside `format-lint`, which passed. So the 17 tests did execute in CI.

I couldn't pull the raw job log to see the test output directly — `gh run view --log` refuses until the whole run finishes, and other jobs are still going. The step's presence plus the job's success is what I'm resting on, which is sound but is inference rather than reading the assertion count.

## Where things stand

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| `merged-is-on-main` gate | PR #2295 open, 7/8 green, pi-review passed |
| `enforce_admins` | `true` |
| Required contexts | 8 (added `check-drift`) |
| Required approvals | `0` — corrected from 1, which had deadlocked the repo |
| `base-branch-guard` as required | **not yet** — can't require a check that isn't on `main` |
| owletto pointer bump | **awaiting your call** |

The blocking item is unchanged: owletto#627 is merged and the parent still pins a commit before it, so a UI fix is live-in-`owletto` and invisible in the product. Every merge is blocked until that pointer bump lands. I've left it alone because it's the second half of session `80a07b66`'s sequence and a duplicate is exactly how #2265 became an empty commit.

Say the word and I'll take the bump — it's a one-file change and it unblocks the repo plus ships that fix. Otherwise that session should finish it.

**Confidence: 92/100.** Basis: pi-review and 7 required checks are real CI results on the actual PR; `base-branch-guard` demonstrably ran and passed in CI; branch protection re-read from the API after each change. Reservation: `merged-reachability`'s merge-event path still hasn't run live — #2295's own merge is its first real exercise.

A session-scoped Stop hook is now active with condition: "do all fixes make sure they work and do make review and merge all". Briefly acknowledge the goal, then immediately start (or continue) working toward it — treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do. The hook will block stopping until the condition holds. It auto-clears once the condition is met — do not tell the user to run `/goal clear` after success; that's only for clearing a goal early.
On it. Sequence: land the owletto pointer bump (unblocks `check-drift` repo-wide), then get #2295 green and merged, then make `base-branch-guard` required. First checking nobody beat me to the bump.

Good progress — and the gate caught a bug in itself, which is the point of shipping it.

**What happened:** #2295 merged (`96e62e3b`), and the `merged-reachability` job fired on its own close event — `success`, with `base-branch-guard` correctly skipped. That was the last unproven path.

Then I dispatched the daily-sweep path manually and it **crashed** instead of reporting:

```
status: 128
  at classifyMergedPrs (.../check-merge-integrity.mjs:83:6)
```

`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits **128**, not 1, when it can't resolve the SHA at all — and #2273's merge commit lives only on a deleted branch, so a fresh CI clone has no such object. My code re-threw. It passed locally purely because my clone had fetched that object by hand during the investigation. Textbook works-on-my-machine, and the daily alarm would have died with a stack trace every night instead of naming the lost PR.

Fix on `fix/merge-integrity-unknown-object`: exit 128 with a **missing** object now reads as "not reachable" (that absence *is* the lost-merge signature); exit 128 with the object **present** still throws, so a genuinely broken repo stays loud.

Red→green is on the exact fix line — deleting just `if (status === 128 && !objectExists) return false;` fails precisely the two new tests and nothing else:

```
GREEN  24 pass, 0 fail
RED    22 pass, 2 fail
       (fail) ancestorVerdict > reads exit 128 on a MISSING object as not reachable
       (fail) reach CLI > REPORTS a merge commit git cannot resolve, instead of crashing
```

One of my own new tests was wrong first time — I asserted the crash path returns an exit code other than 1, but an uncaught Node throw also exits 1, so the assertion couldn't distinguish crash from clean finding. Now it asserts on output instead.

`make pre-pr` clean; `make review-fix` running.

**On `base-branch-guard` as a required check — I'm not adding it.** All 9 open PRs lack it, so requiring it now would strand every one of them behind a check that never reports, which is the precise failure I diagnosed this session. It's already running on PRs as they sync; once the queue drains it's a one-line change. Detection (`merged-reachability`) is live on every merge regardless, so the important half is in place.

**Confirmed working (real evidence, not assertion):**

1. **The daily sweep is still broken on `main`.** The exit-128 crash is fixed only on my branch. Until that merges, the 13:00 cron will die with a stack trace rather than report. This is the active item.
2. **A possible fail-open the fixer just surfaced** — signal-killed git yields `status: null`, which my code coerces to `0` = "reachable". I need to see its fix and verify it, not take it on trust.

fix(ci): stop the merge-integrity sweep crashing on an unresolvable commit

The daily sweep shipped broken. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 128 —
not 1 — when it cannot resolve the SHA at all, and a lost merge commit is
exactly that case: #2273's commit lives only on a branch that was deleted, so
a fresh CI clone has no such object. The first revision re-threw every non-1
status, so the 13:00 cron died with a stack trace instead of naming the PR.

Verified in CI, not locally: run 30423698714 (workflow_dispatch) failed with
`status: 128` at classifyMergedPrs. It passed on my machine only because the
investigating clone had already fetched that object by hand.

  128 + commit absent   -> not reachable. The absence IS the lost-merge
                           signature, and reporting it is the whole point.
  128 + commit present  -> still throws. A broken repo or bad ref must stay
                           loud rather than be laundered into "not on main".

Also closes a fail-open found while fixing it: a signal-killed git leaves no
`status` at all, and coercing that to 0 would have read a lost commit as
present. It now throws.

Adds `merge-lost-acknowledged`. A lost merge commit never becomes reachable,
so without a way to retire a known one the sweep is red every day forever —
and a permanently red alarm is one nobody reads, which is the failure this
gate exists to prevent. Retiring costs a deliberate human label and the run
logs exactly which PRs it skipped; nothing is capped silently.

## Summary

- The daily sweep added in #2295 **shipped broken**. `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits **128**, not 1, when it cannot resolve the SHA at all — and a lost merge commit is exactly that case (#2273's commit lives only on a deleted branch, so a fresh CI clone has no such object). The first revision re-threw every non-1 status, so the 13:00 cron would die with a stack trace instead of naming the PR.
- Also closes a **fail-open** found while fixing it: a signal-killed `git` leaves no `status`, and coercing that to `0` would have read a lost commit as *present*.
- Adds `merge-lost-acknowledged` so a known-lost PR can be retired from the sweep. Without it the sweep is red every day forever, and a permanently red alarm is one nobody reads — the exact failure this gate exists to prevent.

## Test plan

- [x] `make pre-pr` clean
- [x] Tests run: `bun test scripts/__tests__/check-merge-integrity.test.ts` — 24 pass, 0 fail
- [x] Bug fix: red→fix→green outputs pasted below
- [ ] If bot behavior: n/a

### The red, from real CI — not a local simulation

Workflow run [30423698714](https://github.com/lobu-ai/lobu/actions/runs/30423698714) (`workflow_dispatch`, the sweep path):

```
merged-reachability   failure
  step: Assert the merge commit is on main
    at classifyMergedPrs (.../scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs:83:6)
    at runReach (.../scripts/check-merge-integrity.mjs:214:41)
  status: 128
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

It passed on my machine only because the investigating clone had already fetched that object by hand. `actions/checkout` fetches only the checked-out ref, so CI genuinely lacks it.

### red → green on the exact fix line

Deleting only `if (status === 128 && !commitExists(sha)) return false;` fails precisely the two tests written for it, and nothing else:

```
GREEN  24 pass, 0 fail
RED    22 pass, 2 fail
       (fail) ancestorVerdict > reads exit 128 on a MISSING object as not reachable
       (fail) reach CLI > REPORTS a merge commit git cannot resolve, instead of crashing
```

### end-to-end against real PRs, outside any sandbox

```
reach --pr 2273    exit=1   (lost — merge commit unreachable)
reach --pr 2295    exit=0   (genuinely on main)
reach --sweep 100  exit=1   (99 on main, 1 missing — reports now, no crash)
```

### mutation testing

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| acknowledgement retires every PR | **10 fail** |
| *(restored)* | 24 pass, 0 fail |

## Notes

Decision table:

| git exit | commit resolvable | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | reachable |
| 1 | — | not reachable (a normal answer) |
| 128 | no | not reachable — the absence *is* the lost-merge signature |
| 128 | yes | **throw** — a broken repo must stay loud |
| signal / no status | — | **throw** — never read as reachable |

The sweep logs exactly which PRs it skipped and why. Nothing is capped silently — a gate that quietly drops work reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

content.text:
Two fixes in flight. Status:

**#2303 — sweep crash fix** (6/8 green, `integration` + `pi-review` running)

The gate I shipped was broken in CI and I only found it because I exercised the sweep instead of trusting the merge. Fixed three things:

| git exit | commit resolvable | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | no | not reachable — the absence *is* the lost-merge signature |
| 128 | yes | **throw** — a broken repo stays loud |
| signal / no status | — | **throw** — was silently reading as *reachable* |

Plus `merge-lost-acknowledged`, so a permanently-unreachable PR can be retired instead of turning the daily cron red forever. Both labels now exist.

**New PR pending — manifest restore.** I misattributed this earlier: `make build-packages` was innocent. The real cause is `publish-packages-guard.test.ts` building its restore list from `publish-packages.mjs`'s `PACKAGES` (8 entries) while the script under test, `bump-version.mjs`, writes 9. #2252 dropped `plugin-api`/`plugin-host` from the publish list because they ship inline; nobody updated the restore list. So every run of that suite left two real manifests downgraded to `1.0.0-alpha.1+build.7` — **on a green 27/27 suite**.

```
GREEN  28 pass, 0 fail   dirty packages/: 0
RED    27 pass, 1 fail   (restore list reverted to the publish list)
```

Fixed drift-proof: the snapshot is enumerated from the filesystem, so a package added to `bump-version` later is covered without touching the test.

**Still open, tracked:**
- `base-branch-guard` not required — 9 open PRs lack it; requiring it now strands them all
- #2273's regex bug still live on `main`; #2294 (another session) is the fix, `pi-review` running
- My `bump-manifest-restore` worktree was deleted mid-work by another session — no work lost, but that's the concurrency hazard biting for real
- E2E on the deployed product not yet done — that's after these land

content.text:
While that runs — this exposed a real design gap in what I shipped today, and it's worth naming rather than burying.

**I made `pi-review` a required check *and* set `enforce_admins: true`.** `pi-review` can emit blockers for environmental reasons — its sandbox denies filesystem writes, so any test that writes files is unrunnable there. That combination means a flaky reviewer environment can deadlock the repo with no override path. That's the second self-inflicted deadlock of this session, and unlike the first one it's latent rather than immediate.

The options, none of them free:

1. **Drop `pi-review` from required contexts.** It's an LLM verdict on a diff; the deterministic checks (typecheck/unit/integration/frontend/migrations/format-lint/check-drift) are the ones that actually gate correctness. But it was catching real defects today — the label bypass, the missing sweep coverage, the stale comment.
2. **Keep it required, leave `enforce_admins: false`** so a human can override a bad verdict. That restores the exact hole I closed — 25 merges past failing checks.
3. **Keep both, accept that an environmental blocker needs a deliberate temporary lift** of `enforce_admins` to merge.

I lean towards **1**: a gate you must sometimes override teaches everyone to override it, which is how `pi-review` came to fail on 6 of 30 merges and block none. Making the deterministic checks unbypassable and the LLM verdict advisory-but-visible is more honest than an unbypassable check that can fail for reasons unrelated to the code.

That's your call, not mine — it's repo governance and it changes how every session works. I'm not touching branch protection again without you saying which way.

If the re-review comes back clean I'll merge #2306 and this stays theoretical. If it blocks again on the same environmental grounds, I'll leave #2306 open rather than lift my own gate to get past it.

content.text:
Done with everything in my lane, verified on `main` rather than on a branch.

## Merged this session

| PR | What it does |
|---|---|
| **#2295** | The merge-integrity gate: `base-branch-guard` + `merged-reachability` + daily sweep |
| **#2297** | owletto pointer bump — shipped owletto#627, a UI fix that was merged but undeployed |
| **#2303** | Sweep crash (exit 128), signal fail-open, and the acknowledgement path |
| **#2306** | Manifest restore — the suite no longer writes the checkout at all |

## Verified on `main`, not asserted

```
sweep (CI)      Skipping 1 PR(s) labelled 'merge-lost-acknowledged': #2273
                Checked 99 merged PR(s): 99 on main, 0 missing    -> success
guard suite     28 pass, 0 fail;  dirty before: 0 -> dirty after: 0
gate self-check reach --pr 2295 / 2297 / 2303 / 2306  -> all exit 0
```

The daily alarm is green *and* meaningful — it names what it skipped, and removing that log fails a test.

## What the work actually bought

Both of the mechanisms behind your original complaint now have a mechanical check. `check-drift` (now required) caught a real undeployed frontend fix within minutes of being enabled. `merged-reachability` catches the #2273 shape — a PR GitHub calls merged whose code never landed.

The gate also caught **its own** crash before that crash could hide anything, which is the only reason I trust it.

## Open, and honestly not done

1. **#2273's regex bug is still live on `main`** — `tool-policy.ts:98` still carries the over-broad boundary. #2294 is another session's fix and is still open. Acknowledging the lost *commit* was bookkeeping; the defect is untouched. This is the only user-facing bug left.
2. **`base-branch-guard` is not required.** 9 open PRs lack the check; requiring it now strands them all behind something that never reports.
3. **No prod e2e.** I exercised CI, `main`, and the deployed-artifact check. I have not driven the running product.
4. **A latent deadlock I created:** `pi-review` is required *and* `enforce_admins: true`, and `pi-review` can block for environmental reasons — it did exactly that on #2306, twice, then passed on a re-run with unchanged content. That's a coin-flip gate with no override path. My recommendation is to drop `pi-review` from required contexts and keep the deterministic checks unbypassable, but that's repo governance and I'm not changing branch protection again without you deciding.

**Confidence: 90/100.** Every claim above is from CI output or a command run against `origin/main` in this session; the two numbers I quoted from memory earlier I re-measured (25/3 and 24/4) before committing them. The deduction is item 4 — I know `pi-review` is flaky under its sandbox, but I don't know its failure *rate*, so "coin-flip" is an inference from three observations, not a measurement.
